burden.text: Lords start a step less loyal, and recruits refill 15 % slower while new slave soldiers must be bought abroad.

turned.name: Sons of the people

ambitions.name: The Hospitallers' rock

legacy.name: Arsenal of Alexandria
legacy.text: Galleys build 15 % faster and ports raise 20 % more sailors.

ambitions.name: Shield of the Taurus
ambitions.hint: Between the Turkmen and the Nile stand the mountain beyliks.
ambitions.text: Hold Malatya and make Dulkadir your subject.

legacy.name: Taurus forts
legacy.text: Frontier garrisons +25 %, each castle feeds one more ring, mountain marches 10 % faster.

ambitions.name: Keepers of the pilgrim road

ambitions.text: Own the Hejaz and keep Cyprus as your subject.

legacy.name: The mahmal
legacy.text: Muslim countries think one step better of you; tribute +24 %.

ambitions.name: The Franks at Diu

ambitions.text: Hold a fifth of the Malabar trade while Portugal is at sea.

legacy.name: Fleet of Suez

ambitions.text: Know gunpowder infantry and standing regiments.

legacy.name: Fifth corps
legacy.text: Powder mills may be built early; hand gunners deal 6 % more hits.

legacy.name: The Circassian peace
legacy.text: Lords start a step more loyal, stability +1 and 10 % more tax reaches you.

birthright.name: Kitabkhana of Herat
birthright.text: Scholars make 12 % more research, school seats +25 %, officials reach full effect a year sooner, and fleeing scholars favour you.
birthright.why: Under Shah Rukh and Gawhar Shad, Herat became the cultural capital of the Persianate world, with an experienced Persian fiscal bureaucracy (catalogue).

heydays.name: Ulugh Beg's observatory
heydays.text: Observatories, universities and lenses cost 20 % less to research, scholars +10 %, spread discount cap +8.
heydays.why: Ulugh Beg ruled Transoxiana from Samarkand, seat of his observatory and madrasas (catalogue key locations).

heydays.name: Khorasan highway
heydays.text: Traders passing +25 %, land traders gather 15 % more, caravanserais cost a quarter less.
heydays.why: The realm sat on the overland Silk Road Samarkand-Herat-Tabriz and the Herat-Qandahar-Multan road to India, and depended on peace along it.

heydays.name: Mirzas in Hindustan
heydays.text: Commanders may take the Rumi dastur, guns deal 15 % more hits, and you can hold 2 more lords.
heydays.why: A Timurid prince, Babur, driven from Transoxiana by the Uzbeks, turned through Kabul to India (catalogue future path); this heyday is inferred from that line.

burden.name: Every prince an army
burden.text: Appanage princes rule their own courts: lords start a step less loyal and provinces are 20 % further from the throne.
burden.why: Grandsons held Fars, Iraq-i Ajam and Gurgan with their own armies and Ulugh Beg ruled Transoxiana almost alone; succession went by contest (catalogue constraints).

heydays.why: Inferred: steppe armies kept their edge until gunpowder infantry and field guns spread.

legacy.text: Houses of worship convert 25 % faster; your faith thinks one step better of you.

birthright.why: The Ming governed through a very large literate bureaucracy recruited by examination, with ministries in Beijing and a parallel set in Nanjing.

heydays.name: Yu Qian's defence of the capital
heydays.text: Garrisons fight 30 % harder, castles cost a fifth less, and commanders may fight in the wagon-fort style.
heydays.why: After Tumu (1449) Yu Qian held Beijing; the northern garrisons at Datong and Xuanfu and the later border walls became the Ming answer to steppe cavalry.

heydays.name: Jingdezhen blue-and-white
heydays.text: Porcelain output rises 40 %, and Jiangnan's silk looms make 40 % more.
heydays.why: Jingdezhen porcelain and Jiangnan silk were the goods Asia and later Europe wanted most from China.

heydays.name: The Single Whip in silver
heydays.text: 15 % more tax reaches you, tax collectors are 20 % stronger, and Heavy taxes does not count in core provinces.
heydays.why: As Japanese and American silver poured in, Zhang Juzheng's 1570s-80s reforms folded land tax and labour service into one silver payment (inferred fit to this age).

burden.name: The sea ban
burden.text: Traders on sea routes gather 20 % less, and ports raise 10 % fewer sailors.
burden.why: Private overseas trade stayed banned (haijin) after 1433; trade was limited to tribute missions while smuggling and piracy grew.
burden.shed_text: Hold 40% of East China Sea trade, or have 10 more trade ships than you began with.

turned.name: Moon Harbour licences
turned.text: One more trader, and 30 % more traders pass through coastal provinces.

ambitions.name: The emperor in the steppe
ambitions.hint: Whoever holds the gate holds the throne, even with the son of Heaven taken.
ambitions.text: Live through a Tumu crisis without losing Beijing, and end the war with the Oirat.

legacy.name: Capital training divisions
legacy.text: Recruits refill 15 % faster, and standing regiments hold 7 points longer before breaking.

ambitions.name: Change the chiefs for magistrates
ambitions.hint: Where the hereditary chiefs hold their seals, send a man with a brush.
ambitions.text: Hold all of Yunnan and see the Luchuan Tai lords gone.

legacy.name: Registered southwest
legacy.text: Foreign rule fades a quarter faster, and the ruler's tongue spreads 20 % faster.

ambitions.name: All under Heaven
ambitions.hint: Calendars go out, embassies come in.

legacy.name: Seals and calendars
legacy.text: Tribute from subjects rises 30 %, and neighbours think one step better of you.

ambitions.text: Learn Field artillery and Ship-mounted cannon after Jesuits reach the court.

legacy.text: Field artillery, light field artillery and ship-mounted cannon cost a quarter fewer scholar-years.

legacy.text: Herds give 25 % more horses, and your horse hits 10 % harder.

ambitions.name: The mandate holds
ambitions.hint: Seven grievances are read in the north; the dynasty need not end.
ambitions.text: After the Jurchen rising begins, still hold Beijing in 1680 and be at peace.

legacy.name: Restored mandate
legacy.text: +10 legitimacy, a new ruler does not lower lords' loyalty, and Hungry does not count in core provinces.

birthright.name: Hall of Worthies
birthright.text: Scholars research 15 % more, officials reach full effect a year sooner, the realm supports 2 more officials, and Ming thinks a step better of you.
birthright.why: Sejong's Jiphyeonjeon and a centrally appointed, examination-recruited officialdom made Joseon's administration very strong for its size; correct tribute kept Ming close.

heydays.name: Rain gauges and the Farmer's Talk
heydays.text: Core harvests roll a step better, stores rot a quarter less, Hungry does not count in the core, 10 % more core tax arrives, tax collectors +15 %.
heydays.why: Standard rain gauges (1441), farm manuals and the graded Gongbeop land tax of 1444 were Sejong's tools against drought and uneven assessment.

heydays.name: Turtle ships and righteous armies
heydays.text: Turtle ships hit 30 % harder, commanders may use the hwacha battery, and foreign rule lasts 30 % longer in your homeland.
heydays.why: In the Imjin War (1592-1598) Yi Sun-sin's armoured ships, hwacha rocket carts and the volunteer righteous armies wore down the Japanese invasion.

mark.name: Righteous armies
mark.text: Foreign rule lasts 30 % longer in your homeland.

heydays.name: Uniform tribute law
heydays.text: 15 % more tax reaches you, Heavy taxes does not count anywhere, and officials cost 10 % less.
heydays.why: The Daedongbeop (1608-1708) turned county tribute into a land tax in rice and the 1750 equal-service law halved the cloth levy; this is the later Joseon revival (inferred fit to this age).

burden.name: The commoner's service
burden.text: Recruits refill 15 % slower, levies serve a month less before pay, and 5 % less tax reaches you.
burden.why: Military and corvee service fell on commoner men while yangban escaped it, and evasion was growing; Joseon was not organised for large wars.

ambitions.text: Live through a Japanese invasion still holding nine-tenths of Korea, and make peace.

legacy.name: Mountain fortresses
legacy.text: Foreign rule lasts 40 % longer in your homeland, garrisons +20 %, and lost wars no longer lower lords' loyalty.

ambitions.text: Make the So of Tsushima your subject, or see them gone.

legacy.name: Three ports
legacy.text: 20 % more traders pass the coast, ports raise 15 % more sailors, and fisheries give 20 % more food.

ambitions.text: Hold half of Liaodong, or make the Jianzhou your subject.

legacy.name: Border horse markets
legacy.text: Herds give 20 % more horses, and seizing land alarms neighbours a quarter less.

birthright.name: Village registers
birthright.text: Tax reach +10 %, tax collectors +20 %, recruits refill 15 % faster and levies serve 2 months more before pay.
birthright.why: The Lê state rebuilt village commune registers for land, tax and soldiers, and let its peasant soldiers farm in rotation.

heydays.name: Hồng Đức court
heydays.text: Two more officials, officials reach full effect a year sooner, school seats +30 % and scholars +10 %.
heydays.why: Lê Thánh Tông (r.1460-97) built a Confucian bureaucratic state staffed through examinations and gave it the Hồng Đức law code.

heydays.name: Nam tiến
heydays.text: Conquests settle 25 % faster, frontier growth +15 %, the tongue spreads 25 % faster and frontier land harvests one step better.
heydays.why: Inferred from the catalogue's southern path: Viet settlers and the Nguyễn lords pushed south past Champa into the Mekong delta through the 1600s-1700s.

heydays.name: The villages fight
heydays.text: Guerrilla style, foreign rule in your homeland lasts 40 % longer, light troops hit 25 % harder in jungle and recruits refill 10 % faster.
heydays.why: Inferred: the memory of the anti-Ming war and the commune villages, which the catalogue names as sources of cohesion, carried into the resistance to French conquest in the 1880s.

burden.name: Thanh Hóa grandees
burden.text: Two fewer officials before strain; noble lords start one step less loyal.
burden.why: The Lam Sơn 'founding meritorious officials' dominated a court of regents and purges; the catalogue names court coup or regicide as a failure condition.
